title: Renewal Signal Experiments — KPI Lab Logbook
body:
Purpose:
This logbook captures an experimental, lab-style approach to defining and measuring the QBR metrics we care about for renewal conversations: latency, uptime, cost-per-token, and cache hit rate. Instead of a static glossary, this document records measurement choices, edge cases we observed, formulas we tested, and example KPI rows to surface during customer reviews. The goal is a repeatable measurement recipe that CS and SRE can reproduce and present with confidence.

Scope and framing:
- Scope: Hosted API and Dedicated customers (exclude private on-prem customers for now).
- Aggregation levels considered: per-route, per-customer, and global. QBR decks should prefer per-customer numbers (30/90-day windows) and include a global baseline for context.
- Sampling note: For heavy customers we compute exact aggregates; for low-volume customers we sample queries and apply bootstrap CIs to avoid misleading percentages.

Experimental hypotheses (short):
1) 95th percentile latency correlates better with renewal risk than median latency for chat-heavy customers.
2) Cost-per-token spikes are meaningful when correlated with model switches or quantization changes, not just usage growth.
3) Cache hit rate drop-offs are early indicators of prompt schema changes that increase token lengths.

Definitions and measurement recipes (practical):
1) Latency (api_latency_ms):
   - Definition: end-to-end time from request ingestion at edge to first token produced (for latency-sensitive apps we call this TTFOT — time-to-first-output-token). For batch/embedding routes we use time-to-last-byte.
   - Formula (per request): latency_ms = timestamp_first_output - timestamp_request_received.
   - Aggregation per customer: report p50, p90, p95, p99 over 30/90-day sliding windows. Also include median tail ratio = p95/p50.
   - Measurement source: edge logs (request_id, route, customer_id, timestamps). If edge logs are missing first-output timestamps, approximate by server response start time but flag as "approximate".
   - Caveats: streaming responses can obscure accurate TTFOT if front-end buffering occurs. Recommend instrumenting SDKs to mark first token arrival if customer integration allows.

2) Uptime (api_availability_pct):
   - Definition: fraction of successful requests (2xx or expected stream) over total requests; compute service-level availability per customer and per-route.
   - Formula: availability_pct = 100 * (successful_count / total_count).
   - Windowing: daily availability, reported as 30-day rolling average and last 7-day minimum.
   - Incident handling: requests that timed out due to downstream model OOMs or circuit-breaker fallbacks count as failures; requests silently served by fallback models should be tagged separately and excluded from "successful_primary_model" availability stat.

3) Cost per token (cost_per_token_usd):
   - Definition: total billed cost attributed to request processing divided by total tokens billed for the window. For Hosted customers this equals invoice-backed usage; for Dedicated we compute modeled unit cost (infrastructure amortized) per team guidelines.
   - Formula: cost_per_token = total_cost_usd / total_tokens.
   - Attribution: include model variant, quantization profile, and any accelerator surcharge as labeled dimensions.
   - Example: if a customer used 10M tokens and the billed cost (model+inference infra) is $550, cost_per_token = $0.000055.
   - Caveats: prompt-engineering changes that reduce tokens can drive cost_per_token down while preserving value. Also cache hits should reduce billed tokens — see cache section.

4) Cache hit rate (prefix_cache_hit_pct):
   - Definition: fraction of requests (or tokens) where the runtime returned cached KV/prefix segments such that the model did not execute full attention for those tokens.
   - Two common measurements: request-level cache hit (binary hit/miss) and token-level cache coverage (percentage of tokens served from cache). We recommend reporting both.
   - Formulas: request_cache_hit_pct = 100 * (requests_with_cache_hit / total_requests). token_cache_coverage_pct = 100 * (tokens_served_from_cache / total_tokens).
   - Implementation note: require runtime instrumentation to emit cache_hit flags and token_cache_counters per request. If customers use a shim caching layer, align semantics (prefix-only vs KV-cache).

KPI table structure (canonical columns for QBR slides):
- customer_id, customer_name, window_start, window_end, route, model_variant, p50_latency_ms, p90_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, availability_pct_30d, min_availability_7d, cost_per_token_usd, total_tokens, request_cache_hit_pct, token_cache_coverage_pct, notes_action_items

Example KPI row (CSV-style):
customer_id,customer_name,window_start,window_end,route,model_variant,p50_latency_ms,p90_latency_ms,p95_latency_ms,availability_pct_30d,min_availability_7d,cost_per_token_usd,total_tokens,request_cache_hit_pct,token_cache_coverage_pct,notes_action_items
C-321,Acme Retail,2024-12-01,2024-12-31,chat-completion,redwood-v2-7b,120,420,780,99.95,99.90,0.000060,12500000,46.2,28.7,"Investigate 95th latency spike around 2024-12-14; SRE to check kernel selection fallback. CS to recommend session-level caching for high-frequency flows."

Measurement QA checklist (lab-tested):
- Confirm event taxonomy: request_received, model_invocation_start, first_output, last_output, request_finalized. Missing events require approximation and flagging.
- Validate token counting: ensure tokenizer used for accounting matches model tokenizer.
- Verify cost alignment: hosted invoices vs analytics reconciliation within 3% for sample windows.
- Run a synthetic baseline every week: 1000 standardized requests across top routes to detect regressions in p95 latency and cache hit ratio.

Alerting and playbook thresholds (suggested starting points):
- Latency: if p95 increases by >30% week-over-week or absolute p95 > 1s for chat routes, open an ops ticket.
- Availability: if rolling 7-day min availability < 99.5% for a paying customer, escalate to SRE and CS.
- Cost: if cost_per_token increases >50% without corresponding token growth or model change, trigger a cost review.
- Cache: if request_cache_hit_pct drops >20% month-over-month, schedule a prompt schema review with SE/CS.

Guidance for CS narrative in QBRs (how to present):
- Lead with the one-liner: "Availability has been stable at 99.95% over the last 30 days; we observed a transient p95 latency spike on Dec 14 linked to kernel fallback (details attached)."
- Show trend chart for p95 + rolling availability and annotate incidents.
- Include cost-per-token trend and note any model or config changes that explain movement.
- Use cache hit token coverage to tell a usage-efficiency story: higher token coverage -> lower marginal cost and faster responses for repeated prompts.
- Always pair metrics with recommended next steps and ownership.

Operational recipes (quick):
- SQL-ish pseudocode to compute p95 latency per customer/day (pseudo):
  SELECT customer_id, route, date_trunc('day', ts) as day, percentile_cont(0.95) within group (order by latency_ms) as p95_latency_ms
  FROM edge_events
  WHERE ts BETWEEN 'window_start' AND 'window_end' AND event_type = 'request_finalized'
  GROUP BY customer_id, route, day;
- Token counting tip: run tokenizer on a 1% request sample and compare tokenizer counts to runtime counters; store mapping adjustments if off by >1%.

Open questions for next lab cycle:
- Should we show token-level cache coverage or is request-level cache hit sufficient for most renewals? Hypothesis: token coverage correlates better with cost savings narrative. Need to correlate month-over-month cost savings with token coverage samples.
- For Dedicated customers, which amortization model yields the most intuitive cost_per_token number for CS audiences? Fixed infra amortization vs usage-proportional.
- How do we standardize "successful_primary_model" availability when we have automatic fallback to cheaper models? Proposed: present primary-model availability and a separate fallback-rate column.

Appendix: quick checklist for CS reviewer before QBR deck ship:
- Reconcile costs to billing, annotate any non-standard credits.
- Verify anomalies flagged in last 90 days are annotated with RCA links.
- Confirm the model_variant used aligns with the one listed in engineering rollout notes (linked_artifacts).

Notes (lab style):
- 2025-01-22: Added token-level cache coverage metric after customer pilot showed 12% cost improvement when coverage increased by 20%.
- 2025-02-05: Experimented with p95/p50 ratio as a compact tail indicator; found helpful for product-led customers where median is consistently low but tails drive UX complaints.

Action items (next 30 days):
- Diego to produce a reproducible query set and run weekly synthetic baseline (due 2025-03-07).
- Priya to prototype a fallback-rate column for availability (due 2025-03-10).
- Evan to validate tokenizer parity for top 10 customers (due 2025-03-14).

End of logbook entry.
